records.region: Pernambuco and Alagoas, Brazil; Riacho Seco–Paraíba do Meio, Lagoa Manguaba and the southern coastal outlet channels.
records.candidate_name_role: representative downstream river and connected-system identity only
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected northern headward route follows the Riacho Seco corridor west of Caetés, through the Paranatama/Brejão setting and along the western side of Lagoa do Ouro into the Rio Paraíba course. It continues through Quebrangulo, Paulo Jacinto, Viçosa, Cajueiro, Capela and Atalaia, enters Lagoa Manguaba near Pilar, and finishes in the southern lagoon/coastal-channel outlet setting. Six overlapping original map sheets establish ordinary geographic correspondence; municipal primary prose supports the representative Rio Paraíba do Meio name. The selected headwater, lagoon and coastal channels are not all assigned that name.
records.completion_scope: The selected northern headward route follows the Riacho Seco corridor west of Caetés, through the Paranatama/Brejão setting and along the western side of Lagoa do Ouro into the Rio Paraíba course. It continues through Quebrangulo, Paulo Jacinto, Viçosa, Cajueiro, Capela and Atalaia, enters Lagoa Manguaba near Pilar, and finishes in the southern lagoon/coastal-channel outlet setting. Six overlapping original map sheets establish ordinary geographic correspondence; municipal primary prose supports the representative Rio Paraíba do Meio name. The selected headwater, lagoon and coastal channels are not all assigned that name.
records.supported_name_scope: representative downstream river and connected-system identity only

component_scope_limits: The initial tip is geographically covered but not assigned a separate exact spring name; Riacho Seco is the mapped connected headward corridor.
The selected Riacho Seco approach must not be equated with every prose description of the upper Paraíba source. The exact Seco–Paraíba naming boundary is unassigned.

Rio Paraíba on original maps and Rio Paraíba do Meio in the Pilar municipal plan support the downstream representative identity; this does not establish a naming registry record or uniform scalar hydronym.
Lagoa Manguaba is the selected lagoon, distinct from neighboring Lagoa Mundaú. No lagoon or channel is renamed after the representative river.

No material named reservoir crossing is depicted on the selected inland course in the sources read. Nearby impoundments are not assigned to the route by proximity; this is not a current inventory of every small pond or dam.
The terminal is supported as the southern Manguaba/coastal-outlet corridor connected to the Atlantic. No surveyed mouth-point, bank-edge or exact inlet alignment is asserted.

completion_scope.headward_scope: The 1988 Herchmer sheet depicts the selected western feeder and its irregular eastward course into the Owl River below the separately mapped Owl Lake outlet. The initial feeder has no established name in the maps read.
completion_scope.lake_scope: Small unnamed waterbody/channel widenings occur in the headward landscape. No named major lake or reservoir is traversed by the selected route. Fly Lake and Owl Lake are on the northern upstream branch entering the selected shared trunk, and their names are not assigned to the western feeder.
material_junctions_inspected: Unnamed western feeder joining the Owl Lake outlet / Owl River trunk
Owl River continuation through the southern bend and Herchmer railway crossing
Separate tributary channels east of Herchmer and the Silcox Creek junction in the park
Owl River outlet at the tidal-flat coast of Hudson Bay
completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: The Owl River coastal outlet on western Hudson Bay, in the southern part of Wapusk National Park, south of the Broad River outlet and north of the Rupert Creek drainage. Original park cartography shows the coastal tidal-flat setting. The selected endpoint is treated as a generalized coastal terminal, without requiring a precise bank or mouth-vertex match.
completion_scope.scale_note: Corridor and component correspondence, not exact contemporary banks, individual model vertices, every seasonal channel or an official headwater point.

records.region: Manitoba, Canada; unnamed western feeder joining the Owl River below Owl Lake, continuing through Herchmer and Wapusk to Hudson Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative name for the selected unnamed western headward tributary and the connected Owl River trunk to Hudson Bay; not a scalar name for the entire modeled line.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected FID 9021 begins on an unnamed western headward watercourse, joins the Owl River below Owl Lake, follows its pronounced southern bend and then turns northeast through Herchmer and Wapusk National Park to Hudson Bay. Original Manitoba Herchmer cartography covers the headward feeder and its connection to the labeled trunk. Overlapping provincial and Parks Canada original maps continue the trunk across the railway, the park and the coastal outlet. Fly Lake and Owl Lake belong to the separately mapped upstream branch and are not selected lake passages. Owl River is supported as the representative system candidate, while the initial feeder remains unnamed.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative name for the selected unnamed western headward tributary and the connected Owl River trunk to Hudson Bay; not a scalar name for the entire modeled line.

component_scope_limits: Owl River is a supported representative system candidate, not an accepted product name or a uniform scalar label for every selected component.
The western unnamed headwater, Owl Lake outlet, Owl River trunk, tributaries, off-route lakes and Hudson Bay are distinct scopes.
Fly Lake and Owl Lake must not be described as selected through-lakes merely because a prose account describes them as the named river's headwaters.

The Parks Canada map also prints Oho Sipiy beside Owl River. This is retained only as a source-displayed Cree rendering, not independent verification of registry status or an additional accepted model-group name.
No official river length, exact source coordinate, legal park-boundary conclusion or contemporary navigational suitability is inferred.

records.completion_scope: Bounded source reading establishes the eastern receiving drainage, material lower canal/cañada junction, lagoon passage and actual sea outlet. Complete map coverage of the western surroundings is not complete hydrological correspondence: the selected western head-to-General Pirán receiving link remains unresolved. Therefore representative identity and completed scope-hold counts remain false, with source-material-pending as the sole primary status.
records.region: Buenos Aires province, Argentina; unresolved western lowland connector toward General Pirán, then eastern Arroyo Chico drainage, Mar Chiquita lagoon and Atlantic outlet.
records.candidate_name_role: Source-supported named receiving drainage component and provisional system candidate only; the selected western headward connection is not established, so no complete representative-system identity is claimed.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected western El Yatay–Ramos Otero–Las Tres Lomas to General Pirán receiving connection remains unestablished. Original maps depict separate swales, depressions and short channel marks, but broad basin membership and temporary flooding do not prove this particular link.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected eastern drainage corresponds at corridor scale to the Laguna del Maestro–La Argentina receiving system, Cañada del Arroyo Chico / Arroyo Chico o de las Gallinas, its connection with Canal 5, Laguna Mar Chiquita, and the lagoon's southern inlet to the Atlantic. The selected western head near El Yatay and Ramos Otero lies north of the mapped Arroyo Grande and south of the Napaleofú–Chico corridor. Original detailed maps show separate swales, shallow depressions and short drainage marks across this country, but do not establish the selected northeastward receiving connection toward General Pirán. Broad basin membership and known seasonal flooding cannot replace that missing connection. The record remains material pending, rather than a completed name-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: Source-supported named receiving drainage component and provisional system candidate only; the selected western headward connection is not established, so no complete representative-system identity is claimed.

component_scope_limits: Arroyo Chico is a provisional representative candidate grounded in the named receiving drainage, not an accepted name for the whole selected model object.

The maps and primary prose distinguish the Napaleofú–Chico–Méndez drainage, Canal 6, Canal 5, the coastal Cañada del Arroyo Chico or Chico o de las Gallinas, and Laguna Mar Chiquita. Their names are not made interchangeable along every selected reach.
Arroyo Grande is mapped separately south of the selected headward route. Its nearby name and the regional basin title Grande y Dulce do not name this selected model route.
Laguna del Maestro, La Argentina and Mar Chiquita retain their waterbody identities. A generalized model line through their drainage is not evidence that every connecting reach shares one river name.
No precise spring, bank, vertex-level lake passage, modern canal operation, continuous perennial flow, Korean form or formal registry status is established.

completion_scope.headward_scope: The initial southeastern upland route across the northern Chubut–Río Negro boundary is visible as topographic terrain in the original 1:250,000 map, without a depicted watercourse linking its extreme beginning to the downstream mapped feeder. The independent DPA report describes several headwater streams at regional scale but does not select this feeder.
completion_scope.lake_scope: The established middle route is a stream/mallín corridor among several neighboring lagoons. Its selected line is not treated as traversing every nearby lake. In the terminal sector it skirts the eastern side of mapped Cari Laufquen Chica and follows the downstream outlet setting to Cari Laufquen Grande; this is generalized lake-margin/connector correspondence, not exact shoreline or vertex agreement.
material_junctions_inspected: Mapped headward feeder through the Llama-Niyeo and Rucu-Luan valley setting into the north-running trunk
West-side feeder valleys meeting the Puesto de Hornos–Renangueyeu trunk
Ñe-Luan wetland/secondary-branch setting beside the selected main corridor
Southern Chaiful/Pistola/Quetrequile tributary setting along the west-running Maquinchao corridor
Huahuel Niyeo receiving junction in the low belt before Cari Laufquen Chica
Cari Laufquen Chica outlet east of Cerro Ambrosio and continuation into Grande
completion_scope.actual_terminal_setting: The retained endpoint lies inside the mapped eastern/southeastern part of Laguna Cari Laufquen Grande, an endorheic receiving lake. No sea outlet is involved.
unresolved_material_connections: The selected extreme southeastern headward reach and its connection to the blue-channel feeder that continues toward Llama-Niyeo. The inspected 1:250,000 map shows terrain there but does not establish this watercourse link; the attempted 1:100,000 view supplies no cartography.
completion_scope.gap_character: An unresolved headwater connector/source-correspondence gap, not simply a missing hydronym or a demand for exact spring, bank or vertex agreement. Cartographic non-depiction does not demonstrate that a seasonal connection is absent in nature.

records.region: Northern Patagonia, Argentina; unresolved extreme southeastern feeder, Maquinchao trunk and Cari Laufquen Chica–Grande endorheic lake-link system.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative identity of the established north-running and then west-running Maquinchao trunk and its Cari Laufquen lake-link system. The selected extreme southeastern headward feeder has not been connected by sufficiently explicit primary cartography, so the whole selected route is not a completed identity.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected extreme southeastern headward beginning extends beyond the depicted blue-channel feeder. Its upland terrain was inspected, but the needed connection is not established in the 250k original; the 100k view has no cartography and the independent basin synthesis is too coarse to resolve it.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The established selected corridor follows an eastern headward feeder toward Llama-Niyeo and the Rucu-Luan valley, then the Maquinchao wetland and river corridor north through Puesto de Hornos, Renangueyeu and Ñe-Luan. It turns west at Maquinchao, crosses the low tributary and wetland belt toward Cari Laufquen Chica, and continues through the mapped lake-outlet corridor around Cerro Ambrosio into Laguna Cari Laufquen Grande. The extreme southeastern beginning extends beyond the blue-channel network depicted in the inspected historical map. Its upland setting was inspected, but an explicit connection of that selected beginning to the mapped feeder is not established. Broad basin prose and a coarse basin map do not close this material headward gap.
records.supported_name_scope: Provisional representative identity of the established north-running and then west-running Maquinchao trunk and its Cari Laufquen lake-link system. The selected extreme southeastern headward feeder has not been connected by sufficiently explicit primary cartography, so the whole selected route is not a completed identity.

component_scope_limits: Río Maquinchao is printed on original IGN cartography; Arroyo Maquinchao is the DPA usage. Neither is promoted to a formal registry determination.

The candidate identifies the established receiving/mainstem system. It does not resolve the initial southeastern feeder or establish a uniform name for all selected wetland channels and lake passages.
Historical cartography and dated hydrological accounts do not establish present water levels, year-round flow, or current hydraulic conditions.
The unresolved headward connection prevents a completed representative identity and also prevents a completed naming-scope hold.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
